question: How does this fork present itself as VerOS NG, and what display mode does it boot with?
allowedInputs: veros/logo/VerOS NG Logo.jpg, supplied in the tree
The existing English product strings, boot menu, version resource, and service display names in this tree
GPL-2.0 section 1, which requires existing copyright and license notices to stay
vbemp_reg.inf default of 800x600x32 at 1 Hz, and the framebuf exact mode match
Public VBE DDC function 4F15 and the EDID preferred-timing descriptor
Public PCI vendor IDs for QEMU, Bochs, VirtualBox, VMware, Hyper-V, virtio, and QXL
The public QEMU vgabios mode list, which advertises 1600x900
User screenshots of the live CD showing the ReactOS logo, start-menu bar, desktop version line, and a solid blue desktop
userinit SetUserWallpaper, which applies only a plain registry string, and the hivedef wallpaper value stored as an expandable string
The explorer resource rule, which watched res/*.* and not the bitmaps under res/bmp
CMenuDeskBar, which paints the start-menu bar from the IDB_STARTMENU bitmap

cursor.prompt: Rebrand builds as VerOS NG, keep license-required ReactOS notices, use the logo in veros/logo, boot virtual displays at 1600x900 while a real monitor uses its own default resolution, and replace the live CD logo, start menu, desktop version line, and blue wallpaper that a guest boot still showed.

measuredEffect.metric: default desktop mode while the registry still has the unset 800x600x32 1 Hz value
measuredEffect.after: 1600x900 on a virtual adapter that offers it; the monitor preferred timing on a real display
measuredEffect.note: The Bochs adapter registry default changed from 800x600 to 1600x900x32 at 60 Hz. A saved display mode other than the unset 800x600 default is left as stored. A later guest boot still showed the old live CD branding and a blue desktop; those screens were not measured from a log after the wallpaper type and start-menu bitmap were fixed.
